content.comment_body: Hello, I have a [product_name] with model [article_no]. I connected it to 230V, but the screen does not turn on and there's no menu visible. I am new to this area. Could the unit be faulty? Thank you for your help.
Hello. That doesn't seem like a good sign. Could you share the complete part number and possibly a diagram or photo of your wiring setup?

Thanks for your response. The exact reference is [article_no]. I recently attended a programming course, but only used software simulators—I've never actually worked with the hardware before. I believe my wiring is correct, but the device won’t power up. Photos are attached. Thanks again.
Hi [user_name], is there voltage at the socket? Have you checked if the unit was dropped accidentally? You could try carefully opening the device—the connector to the display could have come loose.

Thank you for your response. Yes, I'm certain there’s current at the socket; I've measured it several times. I’ve also opened the device and checked voltage at some power supply components—there are 220 volts inside. I’ve unplugged and reconnected the display module several times, but it still shows no signs of life. Is the unit possibly broken? Any advice for repair? Are there any common electronic components that tend to fail in these devices? Thanks in advance.

Hello, your [product_name] with code [article_no] is quite old. I’m not sure it’s worth repairing since new replacements are quite inexpensive. At most, you could buy the same type with code [article_no] if you don’t have special requirements.

analysis.insight_summary: Forum users encounter issues with an older [product_name]: despite proper power connection, the screen fails to illuminate or show its menu. Users discuss basic troubleshooting such as checking connectors or possible internal damage, but the consensus suggests likely hardware failure because of the unit's age. Inexperienced users find troubleshooting difficult, especially with limited support resources for older models.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the device to power up and present a menu after connecting to a 230V supply. They look for simple troubleshooting advice or information about common failure components.
